_about: The brain's music, Hue scenes and projector for each moment of the night: Jon's cue list of 25 Oct 2026 (docs/cue-list.md), moment by moment, with his notes of 11 Nov 2026. Safe to change: nothing here is a secret. docs/cues-relay.md explains it.

music: a playlist below by its short name (jazz, jazzLow, intense35, intense60, act4), or "off" to stop the music, or null to leave it as it is. Two short names may share one playlist in Music at two volumes.
hue: the name of a scene you made in the Hue app, or null to leave the lights as they are.
projector: "on" or "off" for the projector's plug (the IKEA switch in Apple Home, through the two Projector Murderwin Shortcuts), or null to leave it.
An act's settings hold for every beat of that act unless the beat says otherwise. A phase (the blackout, the power returning) wins over the act and the beat.

The brain only acts when the answer changes, so pressing Next inside an act changes nothing unless this file says so. One exception: while the answer is "off" the stop is sent again each time the night moves on, so the blackout always asks for silence itself.

volume: Music's own volume, 0 to 100, for that playlist. whisper: Music's volume while a cue sound or recording plays. videoHoldSeconds: how long Music stays at a whisper after a chime whose bulletin the Parlour TV plays as video (0: the sheet stops the music for the news beat itself).
drawing: while the Relay Drawing runs in those acts (before the door opens), its music and scene win over the beat; unlocked: the moment the door opens, before the next beat.
cut: on that act and beat, the music is cut the moment the newscast begins (trigger clips: the closing bulletin's first recorded part, the first Name press) and stays off for that beat.
study: in those acts, the playing scene while the study's public state is one of states (a group at the wall), the idle scene when it leaves them.

cake: the Cake! button. The music stops first. Then that one song from the Music library at that volume, with that scene, on the speakers named: "homepods" (every HomePod the Music app can see), "mac" (the Music app's own output), or a list of names from npm start -- --speakers. The sheet's music and scene come back when the song ends, or after seconds if Music cannot be read.

cueSounds: who makes a cue's sound. "screens" (11 Nov 2026): every room screen and every phone plays the chimes, the stings, the scream and bulletin 2's sounder itself, so the brain plays no cue sound: it only speaks bulletin 2's recordings, cueSpeechDelaySeconds after the sounder. "brain": the brain plays every cue from its own speakers as well, as before; beside the screens that is an echo a second late.
strings: the Orangerie string lights in Salem's game (red, green) and the rest of the night (decor). hue 0 to 360, sat and brightness 0 to 100.

musicShortcuts (31 Oct 2026, the formal rundown): with MUSIC_SHORTCUTS=on in cues/.env the music runs through Apple Home instead of the Music app: one Shortcut on the brain per playlist setting, by the same short key, each running a Home scene that plays on the HomePods. A key may list several Shortcuts, run in order: act4 is the house jazz first, then the Study's and the Orangerie's own music, from the first round of Act 4 (the warning and the groups keep the jazz) until dessert.

musicShortcuts.off: the Shortcut that stops the music on all four HomePods. It must exist on the brain under exactly this name: on 11 Nov 2026 it did not, and nothing could stop the music all evening. The brain checks for it when it starts and says so in capitals, and the Host tab says so too.

musicShortcuts.duck (optional): the Shortcut that turns the music down while the brain speaks a recording (bulletin 2 at supper); the setting that was on comes back when it ends. musicShortcuts.cake (optional, not named today): a Shortcut that plays the cake's song on the HomePods, in place of the Music app.
